_source: Hand-maintained. These are the ONLY fields asl does not generate from CPIC.
_note: CPIC publishes clinical_function, biochemical_function, activity_value,
evidence_strength, findings and citations per allele — all of which asl reads
from data/evidence/DPYD_evidence.json and never edits. CPIC does NOT publish
cohort size, cohort ancestry, or any flag for in-vitro/clinical disagreement.
Those three live here.
HARD RULE: nothing in this file may alter a phenotype call, an activity score,
or a clinical action. It is display and flag metadata only, asserted by test
(tests/test_no_conflict_affects_phenotype.py). The 0.7.2 *6 incident is the
reason for that rule: a defensible clinical judgement was written directly
into a pinned data table with nothing recording why, and it survived four
releases as an undeclared deviation from CPIC.
Every entry must state the disagreement in BOTH directions. An entry that
cites only the evidence against CPIC is advocacy, not a conflict record.
pending_guideline_changes records a change CPIC has ANNOUNCED but not yet
published. CPIC deliberately freezes its database until publication, so the
--check drift guard is blind to these by construction: the API still returns
the old value and agrees with the pinned table. The announcement is therefore
the only signal, and it has to be carried by hand until the guideline lands.
Same hard rule applies — this may not alter a phenotype, activity score or
clinical action. It is a flag stating that CPIC's own call is about to move.

c.2194G>A (*6).cpic_position: Normal function, activity 1.0, evidence strength Moderate, basis in vitro (5-fluorouracil), PMID 23328581 (Offer 2013, HEK293T recombinant enzyme).

contradicting_evidence.citation: Del Re M et al. Pharmacogenomics J 2019;19:556
contradicting_evidence.finding: c.2194G>A associated with grade >=3 adverse reactions, OR 1.7, p<0.001. Authors conclude it should be evaluated pre-emptively.

contradicting_evidence.citation: Boige V et al. PETACC-8 secondary analysis, JAMA Oncol 2016
contradicting_evidence.finding: Significant association with severe toxicity on FOLFOX4.

contradicting_evidence.citation: Ruzzo A et al. TOSCA, Br J Cancer 2017
contradicting_evidence.finding: Significant for time to grade >=3 neutropenia.

evidence_supporting_cpic.citation: Baskarane H et al. D-TORCH sub-study, Front Pharmacol 2026;17:1732128
evidence_supporting_cpic.finding: rs1801160 found in 13/76 patients. No significant association between DPYD variant status and grade >=2 toxicity overall (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.26-1.98, p=0.612). Prospective, WES-based, unselected for toxicity.

c.2194G>A (*6).resolution: UNRESOLVED. CPIC has not revised the call. asl reports CPIC's call as CPIC's, and reports this disagreement alongside it. asl does not reclassify the allele.

c.496A>G.cpic_position: Normal function, activity 1.0, evidence strength Moderate, basis in vitro (5-fluorouracil), PMID 24648345 (Offer 2014, HEK293T recombinant enzyme).

contradicting_evidence.citation: Pavithran K et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39(15_suppl):e15517 (ASCO abstract)
contradicting_evidence.finding: 47/375 (12.5%) variant-positive; 32 of those 47 (68.8%) carried c.496A>G. 35/47 developed grade II-III toxicity DESPITE pre-emptive activity-score-guided dose reduction. Reported chi-square association with severe adverse reaction, p=0.002.
contradicting_evidence.caveats: ABSTRACT ONLY — no full paper exists as of 2026-08. The headline statistic '74.5%' is ambiguous between a chi-square value, a proportion of carriers with toxicity, and a sensitivity; it must not be quoted as if its meaning were established.

contradicting_evidence.citation: Gentile G et al. Pharmacogenomics J 2016;16(4):320-325
contradicting_evidence.finding: As part of a three-SNP haplotype (rs1801160 + rs1801265 + rs2297595), reduces 5-FU degradation rate comparably to rs3918290. EX VIVO PBMC assay, NOT clinical toxicity.

contradicting_evidence.citation: Hamzic S et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2021
contradicting_evidence.finding: Effects of c.85T>C and c.496A>G on DPD activity (plasma UH2/U ratio) are HAPLOTYPE-DEPENDENT. Supports a mechanism, not a clinical effect size.

evidence_supporting_cpic.citation: Baskarane H et al. D-TORCH sub-study, Front Pharmacol 2026;17:1732128
evidence_supporting_cpic.finding: rs2297595 found in 7/76 patients with no toxicity signal. Directly contradicts the Pavithran finding, in the same national population, with a stronger method (prospective, WES, unselected for toxicity).

evidence_supporting_cpic.citation: Kanai M et al. Cancer Med 2022
evidence_supporting_cpic.finding: GWAS of fluoropyrimidine toxicity. No significant association for rs1801265; neutropenia OR 0.53, p=0.054, trending protective. Individual common variants were not predictive.

c.496A>G.resolution: CONTESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The two unbiased Indian studies disagree with each other, and the better-conducted one is null. asl reports both sides and reports no elevated risk. This is the allele where an honest conflict record matters most, because it is the one an Indian clinician is most likely to ask about.

c.85T>C (*9A).cpic_position: Normal function, activity 1.0, evidence strength STRONG, basis IN VIVO (dihydrouracil), PMID 18452418.

contradicting_evidence.citation: He YF, Wei W, Zhang X et al. J Clin Pharm Ther 2008;33(3):307-314 — the CPIC citation itself
contradicting_evidence.finding: Plasma DPD activity measured directly; found NO correlation between *9A and DPD activity. This is the basis of CPIC's Normal-function call, and it is an East Asian in-vivo study, not an Indian one and not an in-vitro one.

contradicting_evidence.citation: Varma R et al. Drug Metab Pers Ther 2020;35(4)
contradicting_evidence.finding: GG genotype associated with significantly higher 5-FU plasma levels at 3h post-capecitabine, suggesting impaired elimination. Pharmacokinetic, not toxicity-endpoint.

evidence_supporting_cpic.citation: Kanai M et al. Cancer Med 2022
evidence_supporting_cpic.finding: No toxicity association; trending protective for neutropenia (OR 0.53, p=0.054).

c.85T>C (*9A).resolution: NOT A FUNCTION DISPUTE. This entry exists because *9A is the most common DPYD allele in Central/South Asian populations (CPIC frequency 0.25526) and the evidence for its Normal-function call comes from a 142-patient Chinese cohort. That is a provenance disclosure, not a claim that the call is wrong. asl states the ancestry of the evidence and stops there.

GENTILE_2016_THREE_SNP.citation: Gentile G et al. Pharmacogenomics J 2016;16(4):320-325
GENTILE_2016_THREE_SNP.claim: This three-SNP combination ('Hap7') reduces the 5-FU degradation rate comparably to rs3918290 (*2A), the most severe loss-of-function allele known.
GENTILE_2016_THREE_SNP.what_the_claim_is_not: It is an EX VIVO 5-FU degradation-rate assay in patient PBMCs. It is NOT a clinical toxicity finding, and it is NOT a claim of equivalent toxicity risk to *2A.

clinical_non_replication.citation: Kanai M et al. Cancer Med 2022
clinical_non_replication.finding: No toxicity association for rs1801265; neutropenia OR 0.53, p=0.054, trending protective.

clinical_non_replication.citation: Ruzzo A et al. TOSCA, Br J Cancer 2017
clinical_non_replication.finding: Null for these common variants tested individually.

mechanistic_support.citation: Hamzic S et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2021
mechanistic_support.finding: Effects of c.85T>C and c.496A>G on DPD activity are haplotype-dependent, which is consistent with a haplotype-level effect existing.

GENTILE_2016_THREE_SNP.phase_requirement: Phase cannot be determined from unphased genotypes. This is ALWAYS emitted as a flag with phase_unknown, never as a call.

_note: What class of variant an assay method can detect at all. This is not a
per-allele property, so it cannot be generated from CPIC's allele table:
CPIC publishes what each allele does, not what a given laboratory method
is capable of seeing.
The distinction matters because an SNV-only method reading hom_ref at a
deleted locus is reading the surviving chromosome. One reference copy and
two reference copies are indistinguishable to it, so 'wild type' at that
locus is consistent with both no variant and a whole-exon deletion.

snv_only.detects: single-nucleotide variants and small indels at the assayed positions
snv_only.cannot_detect: copy-number and structural variants (whole-exon or multi-exon deletions, duplications, inversions)
snv_only.why: A genotyping method that reads one base at a time infers zygosity from allele ratio at that base. On a chromosome carrying a deletion of the locus there is nothing to amplify, so the surviving allele reads as homozygous reference. Absence of the deletion is therefore not established by a negative SNV result.

frequency_evidence.citation: van Kuilenburg et al. 2009, Hum Genet 125(5-6):581-590
frequency_evidence.finding: Genomic deletions affecting DPYD were found in 7% (5/72) of DPD-deficient patients. The authors conclude that screening DPD-deficient patients for genomic deletions should be considered.
frequency_evidence.caveats: Denominator is patients already known to be DPD deficient, not an unselected population. This is the proportion of deficiency attributable to deletions, NOT a population carrier frequency, and it must not be read as one.

frequency_evidence.finding: A patient wild type on the 4-variant panel plus c.2194G>A developed grade 4 diarrhoea and septic shock after 8 days of full-dose capecitabine, chemotherapy abandoned. NGS and SNP array found a heterozygous ~500 kb deletion of exons 5-20, containing 4 of the 5 loci the panel had screened. DPD activity was 49% of control with raised plasma uracil and a reduced DHU/U ratio.
frequency_evidence.caveats: Single case report. Establishes the failure mode and its mechanism, not its frequency. The authors note the deletion would have indicated a 50% dose reduction had it been known before treatment.

frequency_evidence.citation: Saarenheimo et al. 2021, Cancer Chemother Pharmacol 87(5):657-663
frequency_evidence.finding: Pre-emptive DPYD screening found a high prevalence of a novel exon 4 deletion in the Finnish population.
frequency_evidence.caveats: Shows that deletion prevalence is population-specific. No equivalent survey has been published for any Indian population, so the local rate is unknown rather than low.

snv_only.population_note: No study has surveyed DPYD structural variants in any Indian population. The rate here is unmeasured, which is not the same as low. Reporting it as either would be an assertion the data does not support.
snv_only.what_asl_does: States that the method could not interrogate this variant class, and that a negative result therefore does not exclude it. Does not estimate a residual probability, does not alter the phenotype, and does not recommend further testing -- what to do about an unexcluded variant class is a clinical decision.
snv_only.detection_methods: Multi-exon deletions require a copy-number-aware method: MLPA, read-depth CNV analysis on NGS, or SNP array. The Delcuratolo case was found by read-depth NGS and confirmed by SNP array.

cnv_aware.detects: single-nucleotide variants, small indels, and copy-number variants at the assayed positions
cnv_aware.what_asl_does: Emits no variant-class limitation flag, because the method interrogated this class.

c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).source: CPIC Comment on Pending DPYD Guideline Update, Whirl-Carrillo M, blog.clinpgx.org, 9 July 2026
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).current_pinned_value: activity value 0.5; heterozygote activity score 1.5; Intermediate Metabolizer; CPIC action REDUCE_50PCT
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).announced_value: activity value 0.75; heterozygote activity score 1.75; recommendation is to initiate cycle 1 at 75% of the intended dose, with careful evaluation for escalation toward standard dosing in subsequent cycles if no clinically significant toxicity
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).scope_limit: CPIC states this change is specific to c.1129-5923C>G (rs75017182, the causal HapB3 allele) and must NOT be applied to other variants that previously shared the same allele value.
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).why_this_matters_here: In CPIC's own Central/South Asian frequency data HapB3 is 0.019658 — 77.5% of the 0.025375 summed frequency of the FOUR variants the EMA/CPIC guideline panel tests, and 60.5% of the 0.032505 summed frequency of EVERY actionable DPYD allele CPIC publishes. Both denominators are stated because the first describes what a guideline-conformant panel can find and the second what the gene can carry; quoting either alone overstates or understates the reach of this change. On either reading HapB3 dominates, so a change to its dose recommendation changes what most Indian panel-positive patients are told.
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).what_asl_does: Reports CPIC's currently published value unchanged, and flags alongside it that CPIC has announced a revision. asl does not pre-apply the announced value: doing so would be an undeclared deviation from the pinned source of truth in the opposite direction from the 0.7.2 *6 incident, and the pre-publication text is not the guideline.
c.1129-5923C>G, c.1236G>A (HapB3).caveat: The 75% figure is from a pre-publication comment, not the final guideline, and CPIC's own database still shows 0.5. Treat the announced value as notice that the recommendation is moving, not as a value to dose on.
